purpose: Expand PFC-01 with staged regional and transregional counter-samples without treating cultures, nations, religions, schools, or famous people as Factorium concepts.
scope_boundary: A broad sampling program, not all philosophy, a world canon, a ranking, or a claim that any lane is internally uniform.
terminology_rules: Use Arabic-language, Islamic, Persianate, and Arab only when the source scope warrants that distinct label.
Treat Indian, South Asian, Hindu, Buddhist, Jain, and Sikh traditions as overlapping but non-interchangeable.
Treat Buddhism as transregional, with Indian, Tibetan, Chinese, Korean, Japanese, Southeast Asian, and contemporary developments retaining location and lineage.
Do not use Eastern as a residual category for everything outside the PFC-01 Western sample.
Treat Russian philosophy as a specific historical lane, not as a proxy for Eastern Europe or Eurasia.
Do not collapse African, Indigenous, Latin American, Caribbean, Central Asian, Southeast Asian, or Oceanic traditions into continental essences.

lanes.label: South Asian Brahmanical, Hindu, Jain, Sikh, and materialist traditions
Buddhist traditions across South, Central, East, and Southeast Asia
Chinese Confucian, Daoist, Mohist, Legalist, Buddhist, and later traditions
Korean and Japanese Confucian, Buddhist, Shinto-related, and modern traditions
Arabic-language, Islamic, and Persianate philosophical traditions
Jewish philosophical traditions across ancient, medieval, and modern settings
Russian and separately identified Eastern European traditions
Regionally and linguistically identified African philosophical traditions
Latin American and Caribbean scholastic, liberation, decolonial, and related traditions
Region-specific Indigenous and First Peoples philosophical traditions
lanes.custody_gate: Use community-authorized or established scholarly sources; do not extract restricted, ceremonial, or decontextualized knowledge.

lanes.label: Central Asian and Southeast Asian traditions not adequately represented by the Buddhist or Islamic lanes
Region-specific Oceanic and Pacific philosophical traditions
lanes.custody_gate: Prefer community-led and regionally grounded sources.

factorization_record_contract.rule: Record every source-supported factoring encountered, including incompatible alternatives and null mappings; do not rewrite a source-local factoring to fit Factorium or another lane.

global_reconciliation.precondition: Freeze the complete ordered inventory and digests of every source-local factoring from PFC-01 and GPC-02 through GPC-08 before proposing alignments.
global_reconciliation.custody_rule: Reconciliation can add alignment records and dispositions but cannot edit, delete, or silently merge source-local factorings.

admission_rules.cross_tradition_gap: A structure recurs in at least three independently sourced tradition packets across at least two lanes, lacks an adequate owner, and survives source, taxonomy, mapping, and product review.
admission_rules.within_tradition_gap: A structure may remain a scoped candidate view when it is important within one tradition but does not pass the cross-tradition owner test.
admission_rules.proper_name_or_school: A person, text, school, nation, religion, or transliterated term is provenance or a scoped route, not a canonical concept solely by fame or recurrence of its label.
admission_rules.translation: No English gloss is treated as exact equivalence without direction, context, and loss.

execution_order: GPC-02 South Asian and transregional Buddhist comparison
GPC-03 Chinese, Korean, and Japanese comparison
GPC-04 Arabic-language, Islamic, Persianate, and Jewish comparison
GPC-05 Russian and Eastern European comparison
GPC-07 Latin American and Caribbean comparison
GPC-08 Indigenous, Central/Southeast Asian, and Oceanic custody-led comparison
GPC-09 one-pass global factoring alignment, conflict retention, recurrence, and Factorium disposition
stop: Complete each lane's frozen packet minimum and retain absences, disputes, and translation losses; add lanes when source review exposes an omitted intellectual region, but never claim exhaustive world coverage.
